theater: 瓜納華托高原與墨西哥城

battle.name: 墨西哥獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 瓜納華托高原與墨西哥城
battle.brief: 一八一〇年九月十六日，瓜納華托多洛雷斯的神父伊達爾戈敲響鐘聲，點燃新西班牙的起義；十一年後伊圖爾維德率三保證軍進入墨西哥城，宣告獨立。西班牙殖民軍的野砲在蒙特克魯塞斯與阿庫爾科的山脊上以霰彈射程打散密集的起義縱隊，也隨城陷落入起義軍手中，被鑄造廠與墨西哥城鑄幣廠翻鑄成街壘上的砲。

kit.name: 野砲
kit.history: 能拆成幾件馬車拉走的砲。它讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是西班牙王國在新西班牙的殖民政府及其軍隊，另一方是後來被整合為聯軍的獨立派起義軍。西班牙一方以國王斐迪南七世的名義行使統治，總督弗朗西斯科·哈維爾·維內加斯於一八一〇年九月十三日發表《新西班牙效忠誓詞》，拒絕承認中央執政委員會；同年四月二十日設立的「墨西哥攝政議會」代行中央權力，總督、宗教裁判所與土生克里奧爾議會三方互相牽制。殖民地的行政體系在墨西哥城、瓜納華托、莫雷洛斯、瓦哈卡、普埃布拉與韋拉克魯斯各自分節運作，港口的貿易稅收是軍費的主要來源。軍隊方面，由本土派來的西班牙常備陸軍——步兵營、砲兵連、蘭塞輕騎與工兵——是作戰骨幹；殖民地民兵即「志願兵」（voluntarios）以城鎮為徵召單位，裝備多取自城市兵工廠與卸港船貨；另有英籍、愛爾蘭籍與義大利籍外籍志願兵編成的「遊擊隊」，攜步槍與卡賓槍，由西班牙軍官率領專職追剿。獨立派方面，戰爭最初由教區網絡點燃：伊達爾戈在多洛雷斯集結數百人，多數只帶削成矛頭的農具與砍刀，莫雷洛斯在米切阿坎編成了更完整的部隊，格雷羅在南部山區游擊；這些隊伍以「起義軍」名義鬆散聯合，成分包括克里奧爾商人與地主的出資、牧師與修士的宣傳與掩護、原住民與混血卡斯塔社群的人力、銀礦工與城鎮工匠，以及走私船隊帶來的火藥與海路。到一八二一年，伊圖爾維德以天主教、獨立與統一三項保證為綱，把這些勢力收編為三保證軍。
countriesEn: The two sides were the colonial government of Spain in New Spain together with its armed forces, and the insurgent armies that were later drawn together into a coalition. On the Spanish side the king of Spain, Ferdinand VII, held nominal sovereignty; the viceroy Francisco Javier Venegas published the Vote of New Spain on 13 September 1810, refusing to recognise the central juntas, and a Regency of Mexico set up on 20 April that year exercised the central authority in his place, with the viceroy, the Inquisition and the creole cabildos pulling against one another. The colonial administration ran in separate compartments in Mexico City, Guanajuato, Morelos, Oaxaca, Puebla and Veracruz, and the customs duties collected at the ports were the army's chief source of money. The military order of battle rested on the Spanish regular army sent from the mainland, its infantry companies, artillery batteries, lancer light cavalry and engineer corps; the colonial militia, the voluntarios, were recruited town by town and drew their equipment from city arsenals and from the cargoes that came ashore; a corps of foreign volunteers, British, Irish and Italian, formed the guerrilla detachment, carrying muskets and carbines under Spanish officers whose business was to hunt down the insurgents. On the insurgent side the war began in the network of parishes: Hidalgo gathered a few hundred men at Dolores, most of them with farm tools sharpened into pikes and with machetes, Morelos raised a more complete force in Michoacán, and Guerrero carried on the fight in the southern mountains. These bands were loosely combined under the name of the army of the insurgents, drawing money from creole merchants and landowners, propaganda and cover from priests and friars, manpower from indigenous communities and from the castas, and the labour of silver miners, town craftsmen and the crews of the smuggling boats that brought in powder and arms. By 1821 Iturbide had drawn these forces together under the three guarantees — the Catholic faith, independence and union — into the Army of the Three Guarantees.
people: 關鍵人物幾乎全出自教會與軍界，且多有被俘殉難的結局。伊達爾戈是瓜納華托多洛雷斯堂區的本堂神父，學養出眾卻長年不得志，一八一〇年九月十六日以敲鐘號召起義，三日後攻取存放全城軍械的阿爾洪迪加堡（Alhóndiga de Granaditas）並放出囚犯；他在蒙特克魯塞斯與阿庫爾科兩戰失利後北逃，十月二十一日在巴漢井（Los Alamitos）被西班牙上校路易斯·德·溫扎加的縱隊連同宗教裁判所合作擒獲，一八一一年七月三十日在奇瓦瓦被槍決，頭顱在瓜納華托城門上懸掛十年。莫雷洛斯接續戰事，一八一〇年十月六日發表《民族情感宣言》，一八一二年九月十三日攻占查普爾特佩克堡與墨西哥城，一八一三年七月六日在阿帕察揚發布《獨立莊嚴宣言》；一八一五年十月二十七日被出賣，次年十二月二十二日在聖路易斯波托西被斬首。格雷羅在南部堅持到一八二一年，與伊圖爾維德會師後共同推進瓜達拉哈拉。伊圖爾維德本是西班牙陸軍軍官，一八二一年二月二十七日組建三保證軍，於皮納爾與阿拉馬達的戰役中取勝，八月二十四日與西班牙總督胡安·奧多諾胡簽訂《科爾多瓦條約》，九月進入墨西哥城並旋即稱帝。西班牙方面的關鍵人物包括在蒙特克魯塞斯擊敗伊達爾戈的費利克斯·瑪麗亞·卡列哈、主持鎮壓的曼努埃爾·德·弗隆，以及巴斯克自由派出身的弗朗西斯科·哈維爾·米納；起義軍一方還有科斯神父主持的東加海軍分遣隊、「瓜爾尼卡」號雙桅船在馬尼拉灣的遠航，以及米耶爾·特蘭在普埃布拉的堅守。
peopleEn: Almost all the decisive figures came from the Church and the army, and most of them ended in captivity or on the scaffold. Hidalgo was the parish priest of Dolores in Guanajuato, a man of learning who had long been passed over for promotion; on 16 September 1810 he rang the church bell to call the rising, and three days later he took the Alhóndiga de Granaditas, the storehouse of the town's whole military store, and set the prisoners free. After his two defeats at Monte de las Cruces and at Aculco he withdrew northward, and on 21 October he was taken at the Wells of Baján, Los Alamitos, by a column under the Spanish colonel Luis de Unzaga acting together with the Inquisition; he was shot at Chihuahua on 30 July 1811, and his head hung over a pike at the gate of Guanajuato for ten years. Morelos carried on the war: on 6 October 1810 he issued the Sentimiento de la Nación, on 13 September 1812 he took the castle of Chapultepec and Mexico City, and on 6 July 1813 he published the Act of Solemn Declaration of Independence at Apatzingán. He was betrayed on 27 October 1815 and beheaded at San Luis Potosí on 22 December of the following year. Guerrero held out in the south until 1821 and, after joining forces with Iturbide, advanced with him on Guadalajara. Iturbide had been an officer in the Spanish army; on 27 February 1821 he formed the Army of the Three Guarantees, won the fighting at Pinal and the Alamada, signed the Treaty of Córdoba with the viceroy Juan O'Donojú on 24 August, entered Mexico City in September and was promptly crowned emperor. On the Spanish side the key men were Félix María Calleja, who beat Hidalgo at Monte de las Cruces, Manuel de Flon, who directed the repression, and Francisco Javier Mina, a Basque liberal who had thrown in his lot with the insurgents. On the insurgent side there were also the naval detachment in the eastern waters under the priest José María Cos, the voyage of the schooner Guarnica to Manila Bay, and the stubborn defence of Puebla by Mier y Terán.
kits: 卡面上的野砲，指可拆成砲架、前車與炮尾數件、用馬匹拖行的野戰砲，它是這場戰爭裡雙方都繞不開的火力節點。西班牙殖民軍配備四磅、六磅、八磅與十二磅銅製滑膛前裝野砲，砲身短、仰角可調，附有車隊與騾隊在驛道上移動，另有射角更大、射程更近的臼砲；每個步兵營配一門六磅砲，砲兵連集中使用四磅砲與十二磅砲。火藥由墨西哥城火藥廠製造，球彈由城內鑄造廠澆鉛，港口封鎖一緊，這兩樣最為吃緊。砲術在實戰中以線列展開：把砲連排在正面或山脊，裝填霰彈作近射，一八一〇年十月三十日的蒙特克魯塞斯之役與十一月二日的阿庫爾科之役，皇家軍把砲連架在山脊，起義軍密集的縱隊在坡下推進時正被這種可計算的射程整批整批打散。起義軍的砲火則是另一番景象：一八一〇年九月二十七日攻下瓜納華托阿爾洪迪加堡後，起義軍繳獲城內儲存的火槍、火藥與一批銅砲，得以在次年攻打奇瓦瓦阿爾洪迪加堡時以砲守城；此後格雷羅部在塔拉爾查帕的皇家財政廠鑄造砲身，墨西哥城鑄幣廠也為莫雷洛斯一八一二至一八一三年據守首都的街壘澆鑄短身砲，另有「加里塔」一類輕型野砲由人抬肩扛，用於鄉間游擊。火器以外，起義軍的骨幹是長矛與砍刀，馬匹與農用牲畜既作騎兵坐騎也作搬運；西班牙軍則以蘭塞騎兵、密集步兵方陣與砲兵協同，並以驛道與莊園補給線維持遠距離作戰。
kitsEn: The field gun on the card face is the piece that can be broken down into gun carriage, limber and trail and dragged by a team, and it was the node of fire that neither side of this war could avoid. The Spanish colonial army was equipped with bronze smoothbore muzzle-loading field guns of four, six, eight and twelve pounds, short in barrel and capable of being laid at different elevations, moving on the roads with their limber wagons and mule teams, together with howitzers of greater angle and shorter range; every infantry company carried a six-pounder, while the batteries concentrated the four-pounders and the twelve-pounders. The powder was made at the powder factory in Mexico City and the round shot was cast in the city's foundries, and when the ports were sealed those two supplies became the tightest pinch of all. The gunnery was deployed in line in practice: the batteries were ranged along a front or a ridge and loaded with canister for short ranges, and at Monte de las Cruces on 30 October 1810 and at Aculco on 2 November the royal army set its batteries on the heights, and the dense columns of insurgents climbing the slope were broken up in whole batches by a range that could be calculated. The insurgent gunnery was a different story. After the Alhóndiga de Granaditas fell on 27 September 1810, the insurgents seized the muskets, the powder and a batch of bronze guns stored in the town, which let them defend the Alhóndiga de Chihuahua with artillery in the following year; from then on Guerrero's men cast gun barrels at the Real Hacienda foundry of Tlalchapa, and the mint of Mexico City also poured short-barrelled pieces for the street barricades with which Morelos held the capital between 1812 and 1813, while light field guns of the garita type, carried on men's shoulders, served the country patrols. Beyond the weapons, the pike and the machete were the backbone of the insurgents, and horses and draught animals served both as mounts and as pack animals; the Spanish army, for its part, combined lancer cavalry, dense infantry squares and artillery, and sustained long operations on the roads and the hacienda supply lines.
tactics: 起義軍的戰術核心是流動與消耗：以神甫的布道把鄉村青年拉進隊伍，用長矛、砍刀與少量火槍的雜湊編隊在高地、沼澤、荊棘林與教堂院牆之間周旋，靠夜襲、伏擊、破壞道路與劫奪西班牙軍的運糧隊維持戰鬥，很少正面會戰；海路方面以走私船運入火藥與武器，港口一被封鎖，起義軍的火力便立刻衰退。西班牙殖民軍的應對是把零散城鎮改為據點，以志願兵守備、以正規軍在稅收與礦區之間巡邏，並組織小股騎兵追蹤；對付據點起義則圍而不攻、切斷糧道、把居民集中於城內。城鎮攻防是全戰役最慘烈的一類：奇瓦瓦阿爾洪迪加堡與瓜納華托阿爾洪迪加堡的守軍在缺水缺糧下堅持數週，最後在缺援中耗盡。一八一二與一八一三年的墨西哥城攻防轉為街壘戰，起義軍以短身砲與長矛在狹窄街巷內分割西班牙縱隊，砲火受限於轉角視線而效力大減。決定勝負的一八二一年皮納爾與阿拉馬達戰役則是典型正面會戰：三保證軍在皮納爾正面強攻，繞到阿拉馬達山脊切斷西班牙退路，才迫使對方談判；隨後的科爾多瓦條約與西班牙守軍撤出墨西哥城，代表從前線滲透轉為政治收編的轉折。
tacticsEn: The core of insurgent tactics was mobility and attrition. The sermons of the priests drew country youths into the ranks, and mixed columns of pikes, machetes and a handful of muskets moved between the heights, the marshes, the thorn scrub and the churchyard walls, sustaining themselves by night attacks, by ambushes, by cutting the roads and by seizing the Spanish convoys, and rarely fighting a set-piece battle. On the sea the smuggling boats carried in powder and arms, and whenever the ports were sealed the firing power of the insurgents declined at once. The Spanish colonial answer was to turn scattered towns into strongpoints, to hold them with the voluntarios, to patrol between the tax posts and the mines with regular troops, and to send small bodies of horse after the insurgents; against a rising in the countryside they blockaded without storming, cut the supply road and concentrated the inhabitants inside the towns. The sieges of towns were the most brutal class of fighting in the war: the garrisons of the Alhóndiga de Chihuahua and of the Alhóndiga de Granaditas held out for weeks without water and without food and were finally spent for want of relief. The fighting in Mexico City in 1812 and 1813 turned into a war of the barricade, the insurgents using short-barrelled guns and pikes to cut the Spanish columns up in the narrow streets, their artillery crippled by the restricted line of sight at the corners. The decisive action of 1821, at Pinal and the Alamada, was a textbook set-piece battle: the Army of the Three Guarantees struck frontally at Pinal and swung round to the ridge of the Alamada to cut the Spanish retreat, and only then was the other side driven to negotiate. The Treaty of Córdoba that followed, and the Spanish evacuation of Mexico City, mark the turn from infiltration on the front line to political absorption.
data: 戰役曠時十一年零兩週，自一八一〇年九月十六日多洛雷斯的起義號召起，至一八二一年九月二十八日墨西哥城舉行首屆獨立慶典。人口方面，一八一〇年的清查顯示新西班牙居民約六百萬至七百萬人，墨西哥城逾十萬人，是美洲最大城市之一；瓜納華托與薩卡特卡斯銀礦的產量在戰前佔新西班牙白銀產出的大宗，戰事與港口封鎖使銀礦加工與外運在十年間大幅萎縮。起義軍起點極小：伊達爾戈初集數百人，多數持矛與砍刀，火槍僅數十支；九月二十七日攻取瓜納華托阿爾洪迪加堡的守軍約一千五百人，防線在城門與圍牆工事中堅持到九月二十八日因斷糧投降，起義軍繳獲的儲存軍械成為其後數年的主要火器來源。兵力對比上，一八一〇年十月的蒙特克魯塞斯與十一月二日的阿庫爾科，起義軍自報逾兩萬人，實際在編約一萬上下且多數未著甲；西班牙方面投入數千人，其中蒙特克魯塞斯一役的皇家軍在卡列哈率領下約兩千至三千人。規模最大的西班牙軍聚集在墨西哥城周邊，一八一二至一八一五年城內守軍約數千。一八二一年三保證軍作戰兵力約八千至九千人，另有米耶爾·特蘭率領的東部軍，最終推動西班牙撤出；戰役末段的行軍縱隊自米切阿坎向北推進約一千公里。
dataEn: The war lasted eleven years and two weeks, from the call to arms at Dolores on 16 September 1810 to the first celebration of independence in Mexico City on 28 September 1821. On population, the count of 1810 gave New Spain somewhere between six and seven million inhabitants; Mexico City had over a hundred thousand people and was one of the largest cities in the Americas. The silver of Guanajuato and Zacatecas had accounted for a large share of the colony's output before the war, and the fighting and the sealing of the ports cut the processing and the export of that silver sharply over the ten years. The insurgents began very small: Hidalgo's first muster was a few hundred men, most of them with pikes and machetes and only a few dozen muskets; the garrison of the Alhóndiga de Granaditas, about fifteen hundred men, held its defences behind the gates and the works of the town until 28 September, when it surrendered for want of food, and the store of arms the insurgents took there became their main source of weapons for the following years. On the numbers of men: at Monte de las Cruces in October 1810 and at Aculco on 2 November the insurgents claimed more than twenty thousand, and the number actually under arms was nearer ten thousand, most of them without armour; the Spanish committed several thousand, of whom about two to three thousand under Calleja fought at Monte de las Cruces. The largest concentration of Spanish troops lay around Mexico City, with several thousand in the city between 1812 and 1815. The Army of the Three Guarantees numbered some eight to nine thousand men in 1821, with the Army of the East under Mier y Terán alongside it, and it was they who finally forced the Spanish out; the marching columns of the closing campaign advanced some thousand kilometres northward from Michoacán.
cause: 起義的根子在一八一〇年春已經埋下：拿破崙在西班牙逼迫斐迪南七世退位並把王位交給約瑟夫·波拿巴，母國長期陷於戰爭，殖民地商人同時失去母國的保護與市場，白銀運不出去、進口布帛價飛漲；卡迪茲會議與一八一二年的西班牙憲法許諾給美洲屬地居民以公民權利，短期內鼓舞了克里奧爾人，卻因「萬民同法」而讓原住民仍負擔人頭稅、混血社群無從受惠的矛盾更加尖銳。一八〇八年九月馬德里起義後各地先後成立執政委員會，一八〇九年維拉斯科爾的秘密結社、一八〇九年十二月瓜納華托的騷動，以及托爾西利奧等地教區的抗命，都顯示反抗已成型；總督維內加斯拒絕承認中央軍政府、於九月十三日發表效忠誓詞，等於堵死了和平改革的路。當局的處置反而火上加油：宗教裁判所指控革命，軍方在各地強徵兵員與馬匹、沒收莊園與教會財產，抽糧與徵稅同時進行，鄉村社會的怨憊因此集中爆發。九月十五日效忠誓詞在多洛雷斯被宣讀，次日伊達爾戈敲鐘應變，一場原本爭取改革與自治的抗爭，自此變成爭取民族獨立的戰爭。
causeEn: The roots of the rising were already in the ground by the spring of 1810. Napoleon had forced Ferdinand VII to abdicate in Spain and set the crown on Joseph Bonaparte; the mother country was at war for years, and the colonial merchants lost both the protection and the market of the metropolis at once, with silver no longer able to move out and imported cloth climbing in price. The Cortes of Cádiz and the Spanish constitution of 1812 promised the inhabitants of the American provinces the rights of citizens, which heartened the creoles in the short run but sharpened the contradiction in which, under the formula of one law for all, the indigenous still paid the head tax and the castas received nothing. After the rising in Madrid in September 1808, juntas were established in one town after another; the secret society at Valladolid in 1809, the tumult in Guanajuato in December 1809 and the disobedience of the parishes around Toluca all showed that resistance had taken shape. By refusing to recognise the central junta and publishing the oath of allegiance on 13 September, the viceroy Venegas closed off the road of peaceful reform. The response of the authorities made matters worse instead of better: the Inquisition charged the revolution, the army everywhere pressed men and horses into service, confiscated estates and church property, and levied grain and taxes at the same time, so that the resentment of the countryside broke out all at once. The oath was read at Dolores on 15 September, and the next day Hidalgo rang the bell in answer; a movement that had begun as a demand for reform and for autonomy became a war for national independence.
impact: 這場戰爭結束了新西班牙的西班牙統治，是美洲大陸繼巴西與拉普拉塔之後第三塊脫離西班牙的殖民地，卻沒有帶來穩定。一八二二年伊圖爾維德稱帝建立墨西哥第一帝國，兩年後退位，一八二四年聯邦共和國成立並頒布新憲法，三項保證成為此後墨西哥國家意識的骨架；然而廢黜皇帝與建立共和的過程本身引發新的內戰，此後半個多世紀是卡德納斯、華雷斯與迪亞斯等人輪流執政的考迪羅政治，直到一九一〇年建國百年紀念與一八二三年廢奴法令這類節點才略為定形。北方割讓是另一條長尾：得州、新墨西哥與上加利福尼亞在墨西哥戰爭與美國的購地擴張中逐步失落，聯邦得到佛羅里達，而伊圖爾維德與格雷羅在一八二一年瓜達拉哈拉會議上對北方邊界達成默契。遠洋方面，一八一九年的《亞當斯—奧尼斯條約》劃定北界，墨西哥承認得州割讓，太平洋岸線的爭端延續到一八四八年。此外，墨西哥的遠征使團一八一五至一八一七年抵達馬尼拉要求承認獨立卻告失敗，菲律賓因此落入美國之手，墨西哥在亞洲的殖民地夢想自此斷折。戰爭還留下一筆軍備的帳：新共和國建軍之初，只能以殖民地時期留下的銅砲與燧發步槍充作軍備，這套裝備的射程與精度，反過來規定了她此後對外用兵的樣貌。
impactEn: This war ended Spanish rule in New Spain and produced the third territory after Brazil and the Río de la Plata to break away from Spain in the American mainland, but it brought no stability. Iturbide was crowned in 1822 and founded the First Mexican Empire, abdicated two years later, and in 1824 the federal republic was established with a new constitution, the three guarantees becoming the frame of Mexican national consciousness for all that followed. Yet the very process of dethroning the emperor and building a republic called forth new civil wars, and for more than half a century the country was governed by caudillos in turn, Cárdenas, Juárez and Díaz among them, with moments such as the centenary of 1910 and the abolition decree of 1823 giving the country some of its shape. The loss of the north is a longer tail: Texas, New Mexico and Upper California slipped away in the Mexican war and in American land purchases, the United States received Florida, and Iturbide and Guerrero reached an understanding on the northern frontier at the conference of Guadalajara in 1821. On the ocean the Adams-Onís Treaty of 1819 fixed the northern line, Mexico conceded Texas, and the dispute over the Pacific coast ran on until 1848. The Mexican expedition that reached Manila between 1815 and 1817 to ask for the recognition of independence failed, and the Philippines passed to the United States instead, so that Mexico's colonial dream in Asia was broken for good. The war also left a bill in arms: when the new republic set about raising an army it had nothing to use but the bronze guns and the flintlock muskets of the colonial period, and the range and accuracy of that equipment went on to shape the form she would take in war abroad.
result: 結果是西班牙在美洲大陸的統治崩潰，但收場是由談判而非全勝決定。獨立軍在瓜納華托、奇瓦瓦、米切阿坎、瓦哈卡與阿卡普爾科一線相連，最後一八一〇年代起自南部與海岸收縮西班牙的據點；一八二一年二月二十二日至二十四日的皮納爾與阿拉馬達戰役中，三保證軍正面擊破西班牙縱隊、切斷退路，迫使總督奧多諾胡赴科爾多瓦談判；四月二十七日米耶爾·特蘭的東部軍進入普埃布拉，八月二十四日《科爾多瓦條約》承認墨西哥獨立，西班牙軍隊於九月中旬撤出墨西哥城，九月二十七日三保證軍入城，二十八日在阿爾梅達廣場與主教座堂舉行首屆獨立慶典。最初的起義領袖幾乎全部犧牲：伊達爾戈與莫雷洛斯皆被處決，格雷羅與伊圖爾維德在拿不出像樣軍隊的局面下改以政治手腕收編舊軍，說明戰爭的勝利並非全靠會戰。港口要塞始終未能被起義軍強攻奪取，韋拉克魯斯與聖胡安德烏盧阿的砲台直到撤退時仍完整，維拉克魯斯港的封鎖線與大西洋航運的船隊在此後數十年仍由新政府必須處理。其後是政治收尾期：一八二二年伊圖爾維德加冕，四年內王朝崩潰，一八二四年第一聯邦憲法取代帝制，自此墨西哥在獨立的框架內陷入漫長內戰。一八二二年西班牙曾自古巴派遠征軍企圖收復墨西哥，該軍於一八二三年的西拉戈爾達一役被共和派擊潰，至此舊殖民地的復辟企圖才真正斷絕。
resultEn: The result was the collapse of Spanish rule on the American mainland, but the ending was settled by negotiation rather than by a complete victory. The insurgent armies were joined up along the line of Guanajuato, Chihuahua, Michoacán, Oaxaca and Acapulco, and from the eighteen-tens onwards they squeezed the Spanish outposts from the south and from the coast. In the fighting at Pinal and the Alamada on 22 to 24 February 1821 the Army of the Three Guarantees broke the Spanish columns in front and cut their retreat, driving the viceroy O'Donojú to the conference table at Córdoba; on 27 April the Army of the East under Mier y Terán entered Puebla, on 24 August the Treaty of Córdoba acknowledged Mexican independence, the Spanish troops evacuated Mexico City in the middle of September, the Army of the Three Guarantees entered on 27 September, and the first celebration of independence was held in the Alameda and the cathedral on the 28th. Almost all the first leaders of the rising were sacrificed: Hidalgo and Morelos were both executed, and Guerrero and Iturbide, unable to show a proper army, fell back on political arts to absorb the old forces, which shows that the victory was not won in the battlefields alone. The coastal fortresses were never taken by assault, and the batteries at Veracruz and San Juan de Ulúa were still intact when the troops withdrew, so that the blockade of the port of Veracruz and the Atlantic shipping had to be dealt with by the new government for decades afterwards. What followed was a political epilogue: Iturbide was crowned in 1822, the dynasty collapsed within four years, and the First Federal Constitution of 1824 replaced the empire, leaving Mexico inside the frame of independence and locked in a long civil war. In 1822 Spain sent a reconquest expedition from Cuba to recover Mexico; it was destroyed by the republican army at Sierra Gorda in 1823, and only then did the old colonial counter-offensive come truly to an end.
